steps.content: [Deep Sea]

Step by step, you wade into the Black Tide, the hemp rope around your waist your only tether to safety. The ice-cold water climbs relentlessly—past your ankles, swallowing your waist, rising over your chest—until you are no longer walking but floating, adrift in the Black Tide.
You swim with painstaking caution, skimming the surface, desperate not to disturb what slumbers in the depths.
Your mind fixates on a single number: fifty meters. A grueling distance for someone starved and hunted, but for a rescue boat, it will be a brief dash to shore.
At what you hope is the right point, you draw a sharp breath, grip the rope firmly, and plunge into the darkness below.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: When we were first trapped, the lighthouse keepers gathered every vessel to break through the Black Tide. But the Mania field scrambled our navigation... monsters swarmed every hull. Not a single ship made it out.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: This rescue boat is all we have left. It was the smallest one. We couldn't risk losing it, too. Miles named it the Crippled Dawg. We'd take it out sometimes to collect floating debris, scavenging for anything useful.

The moment you see it, you understand the grim irony of its name: the Crippled Dawg. The rescue boat lies on its side, surrounded by dormant monsters, its hull split open like a fresh wound. Only half an engine remains, a testament to its final collapse.

A deathly silence envelops you. Thin rays of daylight pierce the murky water, illuminating a graveyard of twisted metal seats, a dashboard veined with shattered glass, and thick cables that hang like the suspended tentacles of some long-dead beast.
You hold your breath, extending a thick-gloved hand toward a corner of the cabin. There, half-buried in silt and debris, lies a metal box, its sharp edges just visible above the muck.
Cautiously brushing aside floating debris, your focus narrows to the crank handle on the box's side. This is it: the prize you risked everything for.

On the handle's grip, a massive charred handprint is seared deep into the metal. The impression is so vivid you can trace the outlines of every knuckle and palm bone, a permanent scream frozen in steel.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I saw something was wrong from the top of the lighthouse, even before the Crippled Dawg ran aground...
[Flashback] [Lighthouse Top]

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Miles—!! Speed up! The tide's coming in! Hurry!

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I kept signaling him with the beacon. But that orange glow on the water... it just didn't move.
[Boat Cabin]

steps.speaker: Miles
steps.content: Damn it... of all the lousy timing...

The engine gave a final, sputtering cough, its death rattle a spray of electrical sparks before it fell completely silent. Even the backup batteries were mute, their indicators dark—victims of the corrosive Black Tide.

steps.speaker: Miles
steps.content: The kids back home are probably starving. I'm not letting these supplies end up as monster chow.

steps.speaker: Miles
steps.content: You think a little trouble like this can stop this old salt? I've weathered the Black Tide before!
[Lighthouse Top]

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: It's moving!

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I immediately ran to shore to meet him. At the time, I didn't even stop to think how he'd gotten the stranded boat moving again.
Didn't you say there was a hand-crank generator on the boat?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: It's just a rescue boat. A normal person could have cranked until they collapsed and gotten nowhere. But Miles was different. He was a soldier. He had the power the battlefield gave us.
The Rancor.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Yes. He gave himself to the blade.
[Boat Cabin]

Wedged between the generator and the cabin wall like a human lever, Miles braced his feet and gripped the twisted crank. His hands, calloused from a lifetime of spatulas, now faced a different kind of heat.

As he turned the crank relentlessly, Mania took hold, integrating his body with the boat's systems. It was a parasitic connection; the blade indiscriminately devoured his life force, converting it into a surge of power.

The cost was immediate and horrific: his skin blistered, smoked, and blackened. Agony threatened to unmoor his mind, but willpower held it at bay. He watched, detached, as his own blood and scalding fat dripped onto the generator with a sickening hiss.

steps.speaker: Miles
steps.content: Hah! Now I'm smelling like roasted meat! That's it—now turn! FASTER!

steps.speaker: Miles
steps.content: ...POWER—!!! TURN, YOU HUNK OF JUNK! BURN MY BLOOD TO STEAM—I'M GETTING—BACK—!!!
[End of Flashback] [Deep Sea]
With your last breath burning in your lungs, you dive to the cabin floor and clutch the heavy metal box. There, you come face to face with the island's chef and captain of the Crippled Dawg—Miles.
[Silhouette of a Bloated Body]

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: When the boat stopped moving out there, I had to swim to it.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I found him in the cabin. His body was still making the cranking motion, hands fused to the handle. But he was already gone.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Water and monsters were pouring in. I couldn't take him with me. All I could take was what he'd gathered: one can of luncheon meat, two bloated cans of expired fish, and some waterlogged hardtack. Must have been relief supplies, dropped by other outposts early in the war and carried here by the tide.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: That's what he died for... and we ate it all in one night.

Miles's body is grotesquely bloated, skin straining against the uniform, hands forever frozen in a desperate grasp. Though ravaged by years in the sea, a ghost of a smile remains on his corroded face.

Your oxygen is critically low. You kick off the bottom, struggling toward the surface with the heavy box. After two frantic kicks, a primal sense screams that something is approaching from the murk behind you.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Do you know what happens to soldiers like Miles when they surrender completely to the Rancors?
You glance back, only to find nothing but swirling darkness. Then...
A pitch-black, bloated figure erupts from the gloom. Before you can process it, a putrid, blood-tinged slime floods your nostrils.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: They lose their minds. Their bodies are consumed by that evil power.
The next moment, two hollow eye sockets lock onto yours. It's Miles, his form now a rotting, contaminated horror, pressing against you.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: They become just like the Tide Crawlers... Mania monsters.
